gaps.name: priority-and-creation-order
gaps.observed: workers selected in stable id order ['impl-one', 'impl-two']
gaps.reason: submission and worker-pool schemas carry no priority field; stage ids are visited sorted and workers ordered by worker id
gaps.required: priority pool with affinity before creation order and creation-order tie-breaking

gaps.name: explicit-fallback
gaps.observed: a second compatible worker was chosen: ['impl-one', 'impl-two']
gaps.reason: scheduler.reserve implements soft affinity and records selection_outcome=fallback automatically when the preferred worker is occupied
gaps.required: an explicit fallback decision rather than automatic selection

gaps.name: composed-continuation
gaps.reason: composed implementation eligibility is restricted to the binding's source_worker_id before reservation, so a replacement worker here proves nothing about a composed correction
gaps.required: separate observations of emergency pool activation, automatic worker fallback and fresh provider-session creation

gaps.name: teams-and-repository-bindings-at-the-unit-pool
gaps.observed: 5 distinct canonical principals, one per configured worker, and two declared test scopes inside one checkout
gaps.reason: THIS UNIT POOL decides capacity on canonical principals and carries no Authority team membership, and its test_scope is a declared directory list inside one checkout rather than an independent repository binding. The composed document DOES configure two independent repository bindings and two canonical targets -- see test_two_independent_repository_bindings_are_configured -- so this gap is about this pool's visibility, not about the facts being absent from the system
gaps.required: configured Authority teams with their own scope/capability decisions, and two independent repository bindings proved by a refused wrong repository
